newsitem.title: CANADA: Gendis puts retail chain into bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Gendis puts retail chain into bankruptcy.

text.p: Gendis Inc said on Tuesday that it had withdrawn all financial support for its struggling retail operator MMG Montreal, putting the 169-store chain into voluntary bankruptcy with the loss of 1,462 jobs.
Gendis said that the decision will not affect the company's 227 SAAN or 26 Red Apple clothing stores.
Despite making many attempts to stem "substantial" losses, MMG's sales are not sufficient to support its infrastructure, said G. Allan MacKenzie, Gendis' president.
"As MMG's banker, Gendis has funded MMG's operating losses," MacKenzie added.
MMG operates junior department and family clothing stores in all 10 provinces under the Metropolitan, Met, MetMart, Greenberg and Red Apple/Pomme Rouge banners.
MMG's head office in Montreal also will be shut and SAAN's network of 322 stores will be run from SAAN's head office in Winnipeg, said Bob Whitney, president and chief operating officer of SAAN.
Gendis said that SAAN had made a bid to acquire 89 of MMG's stores, while the remaining 80 are considered to be unprofitable and will be closed.
The new 342-SAAN store chain will employ 4,700 Canadians.
Gendis' decision involves the closure of the MMG head office in Montreal. Of the 322 employees there, about 60 are being offered employment in Winnipeg.

A total of 1,200 full- and part-time jobs will be cut as the result of the closure of the 80 MMG stores. In addition, another 30 employees of Gendis Business Services in Montreal would be affected by the move.

"We recently informed our shareholders that the improvement of our retail operations was a top priority, and we believe today's rationalization of our retail chains provides the solution," MacKenzie said.
Gendis said the revitalized chain is expected to generate sales of more than C$400 million.
